pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs:806 An agent ACCEPT above the owner's in-person threshold is refused in code with the closed owner_approval code, so the gate lives in the substrate the tool call passes through, not in the prompt.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:535 A pending grant lists tools but every tools/call is refused until the host calls enable(); the model has no path to flip enabled.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:226 Grant is keyed to the AgentScope tuple (deal, role, category) plus run, expires after SESSION_SECS, and revoke removes it so the next request at the gate finds it gone (handle() re-reads the session per request).
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:546 Headless agent: a tool outside the role's closed catalog, a malformed call or an over-budget call is refused with a code and audited, never prompted and never passed.
crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:44 Missing (or stale) market reference falls to ASK, not CLEAR; the unreadable case is never spelled as the mild bucket.
crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:67 The model assessor's verdict can only raise caution over the deterministic rules; it has no expression that admits on its own.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:359 The only way the shopper model reaches the owner is a declared tool in its role's closed catalog; the set of doors is enumerable from catalog().

crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs:1072 The signed band is the fixed tier: supplied to the model read-only via table_view and enforced at send_offer; offers inside it need no gate. A separate amendable-plan record is not modelled.
crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:407 Playbooks are fixed in Rust per role/side; no third-party-authored agent definition carrying approval config is loaded.
